claim: A whole-group reading with consist of is said to preclude plural agreement.
evidence_summary: Rickman (2018, p. 42) acknowledges authentic examples of the committee consist of. Swansea’s committee consist of 9 members gives the full composition predicate, whose subject denotes the group taken as a whole.
finding: Plural agreement occurs with the whole-group predicate CGEL uses to exclude it. Rickman credits a reviewer for the examples. Neither that acknowledgment nor the club webpages supply a frequency estimate.
inference: Does applying to a group as a whole exclude plural agreement on consist?

evidence.source: Paul Rickman (2018). Collective nouns and number agreement in New Zealand English. New Zealand Studies in Applied Linguistics 24(1), 40–55.
evidence.passage: §18.2, p. 502, [10i] and preceding paragraph. CGEL treats plural agreement as excluded with a predicate applicable to the group as a whole. Its test uses consist of.
evidence.example: Rickman credits a reviewer with supplying authentic counterexamples, including the abbreviated the committee consist of … .
evidence.establishes: A published acknowledgment of occurrence. The cited examples have no reported frequency or assigned variety here.

evidence.passage: §18.2, p. 502, [10i] and preceding paragraph. CGEL treats plural agreement as excluded with a predicate applicable to the group as a whole. Its test uses consist of.
evidence.example: “Our committee consist of 9 members.” The number gives the membership of the whole committee.
evidence.establishes: Direct attestation of plural agreement in a British club description.
evidence.locator: The ‘Who are we?’ bit, third bullet.

evidence.locator: Second paragraph, sentence listing the officers.
